title: continuity-pocket-playbook
content:
Purpose: tiny, portable set of reminders and temporary steps for bridging an active watch to the next person. Not canonical — strip into Confluence later if anything sticks.

Quick context (TL;DR):
- Last 24h: intermittent 503s from model-proxy when batched requests > 3s; root cause likely buffer saturation on the NLB during autoscale events. Mitigation applied (22:40 UTC): reduced batch window to 50ms on routing policy for hosted-api-prod.
- Current active items: degraded tail-latency on eu-west-1; one customer-facing SLA alert open (JIRA-7821).

Immediate things for next watcher to check at start:
1) Alerts dashboard -> check "proxy-tail-latency" graph for spikes > 95th percentile. (dashboard: /dashboards/proxy-latency)
2) Pager duty/Slack -> review #sre-oncall for any fresh pings.
3) Confirm autoscaler status: kubectl -n inference get hpa,deploy | grep model-proxy
4) Verify canary fallback route: curl -v -H 'x-deploy:canary' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=text-small

Fast recovery checklist (if 503 surge returns):
- Short-term (under 10m):
  * Temporarily switch routing policy to low-burst (CLI: redwoodctl routes update routing-policy --name hosted-api-prod --policy low-burst)
  * Scale replica count up for proxy nodes: kubectl -n inference scale deployment/model-proxy --replicas=6
  * If NLB error rates still high, flip to fallback-region: redwoodctl failover set --route hosted-api-prod --region eu-central-1
- Medium-term (10m-2h):
  * Re-open autoscaler logs: kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-proxy --since=2h | rg "scale"
  * Check GC/heap churn on proxy (new relic: proxy-prod > JVM metrics)
  * Run a controlled load test from staging to evaluate batch window settings: /tools/loadtest --target https://staging.redwood.ai --qps 100 --payload small

Operational gotchas (notes to self):
- There is a stale runbook snippet in Confluence that suggests tweaking read_timeout on the NLB — we removed that behavior last quarter; avoid that change unless SRE lead signs off.
- When scaling replicas, make sure the model-serving pool has capacity; otherwise the autoscaler will spin up but the requests will queue and latency worsens. Check GCP quota: cloudconsole -> IAM & Admin -> Quotas -> GPUs.
- Temporary config is persisted in Vault path secret/ops/oncall/temp-routes; tag changes with ticket id.

Escalation matrix (short):
- If customer SLA breach imminent (>=2 customers impacted for >30m): escalate to oncall-sre-senior and notify CS: cs-incident@redwood.com.
- For infra-level root cause (networking/NLB): ping infra-cc and page the networking lead (Marcus Chen).

Common commands (quick copy):
- Check proxy pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-proxy -o wide
- Tail logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-proxy -f --since=20m
- Cutover route: redwoodctl routes promote --from hosted-api-prod-lowburst --to hosted-api-prod

One-off helpful snippets (cribbed from past incidents):
- Dump KV cache health: redis-cli -h redis-primary.redwood.svc cluster info | rg 'cluster_state\|used_memory'
- Clear prefix cache for a customer: redwoodctl cache flush --prefix customer:acme-123 --confirm

Open questions / TODOs (to grab during the watch):
- Is the batch-window reduction a permanent win for the eu-west traffic profile? If not, we need controlled evals using the Optimize tooling.
- Request a postmortem if JIRA-7821 remains open past business hours. I usually start the timeline notes in the ticket.
- Verify whether the model variant fallback adds any tokenization overhead that could explain the tail-latency.

Hand-off script (what I say when paging the next person):
- "Hey, Aisha handing off — we've got intermittent 503s on hosted-api-prod, mitigated by reducing batch window. Active Jira 7821. If you see >10% 503s over a 15m window, run the short-term steps in the pocket playbook and page Marcus if NLB errors persist."

Notes to self (style + housekeeping):
- Keep this doc minimal — move stable items to Confluence under /playbooks/continuity.
- When closing the watch, add a 3-line summary to JIRA-7821 and set status -> needs-postmortem if root cause unknown.

Scratch area (quick noise I use to triage):
- last-deploy: 2026-03-11T17:04Z (deploy/model-proxy@v2.3.7)
- recent changes: batch-window default 100ms -> 50ms (temp)
- oddity: sporadic increase in 429s on reranker route at ~03:00 UTC; correlate with cron jobs (db-compact)

References:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234SRE/p1678457 (search: "proxy tail latency")
- JIRA: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/JIRA-7821

End of pocket-playbook. Keep terse, and add any live commands you ran to the Jira timeline.

-- Aisha (oncall, notes)
